posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
Silverleaf:

I can't quite shake the feeling of "I don't get this". 

 

Many of us have come to our knowledge of GtG through Sentinels of the Multiverse, but I think it's useful to keep in mind that Greater Than Games has always been about building a game company, not just about building on the success of SotM. At first, SotM was the only product and so it had taken the spotlight, but I think we should all be expecting that we will see many different kinds of things from GtGs. 

 

Also, one of the creators of Story Wars was in the booth next to GtGs at PAX Aus 2013. They became friends and built a business relationship. Knowing that, it seems like a natural step to test the waters to combine the Story of Sentinel Comics with Story Wars and see whether or not there is a market.

 

Is this particular Kickstarter very exciting to me? Not, really, but I think this is a worthwhile project for the company to try. Like I said, I think Story Wars is a good game – it's just not for me. Am I excited about buying a paper version of the comic and paying for shipping? Not really, but I'll go check out the prices and maybe I'll commit. Assuming that the company is going to do this project at some point, was this the right time, or should they have put something out that's more what their current customers are clamoring for? Well, WCOS is about to ship, Tactics just had its first tournament, and Spirit Island has been announced, so why isn't this the right time? Fans of other Sentinels and co-op games have plenty to chew on.

 

The point I want to make is that I'm neither surprised/upset that they are putting out a product that's not to my taste nor surprised that they are putting out a Story Wars related product, and I think that inclusion of a comic with Story Wars makes sense and that I appreciate that they've provided a way to get just the comic.

 

AFTERWORD: I wrote everything above before looking at the Kickstarter itself! Didn't realize they mention meeting Tom at PAX in the Kickstarter description.

Well, Sentinel Conflict will consist of 60 characters, 30 items, and 20 environments.  With current stretch goals, there will be 4 additional cards of some combination of those types, plus 3 objective cards.  Looking at the Multiverse page on the website, there are 23 heroes and 22 villains (counting Vengeance Blade as the same "character" as base Blade) if promos aren't counted, and 14 environments.  WCos plus the preorder bonuses will add 3 heroes, 5 villains, and 3 environments.  That means they only need to have 7 more characters and 3 more environments (there are more than enough items in the game to handle that requirement already) plus a potential 4 choices between those three categories.  They could certainly develop characters and environments (if they don't already have the ideas in place) for both games simultaneously, and there aren't that many that need to be created.

Story War just doesn't feel like it fits >G terribly well, and I don't want a company that makes games that I really like (disclaimer: I haven't actually played a full game of GSF so I can't assess that one) to end up associated with inferior products. While I have no interest in the Story Wars game itself, having a storytelling game based around conflict between characters using items in environments seems to me like the Sentinels IP would fit in perfectly.  For people who like that style of game, I think the lore behind the Sentinels IP will be a great new theme for them.  As far as >G as a company rather than specifically the creators of SotM, well, we've seen that they're interested in growing the segment of their business that focuses on game publishing, so this is a new step in that direction.

Like I said, it isn't to my tastes, but I think it does make perfectly good sense.

posts.name: ViolentSilence
posts.cooked:
The danger is one of brand equity, both for >G and the Sentinels Line. I remember back growing up when a computer game that was a movie tie-in tended to be shoddy, so after a while, you just avoided them unless they got a good review. As it stands, this game sounds like it won't appeal to many people who are already Sentinels players, may put off gamers who are on the fence about the Sentinels, and I can't see how this would appeal to people who don't know the Sentinels lore (certainly not in the way that people might casually know the Marvel/DC stories). For me, the strength of >G is the storylore that the games themselves delivers, not so much in game design (Both SotM and GSF can both be very heavy on book-keeping, so can be clunky at times), so I'd worry about a game that sounds very weak mechanically further damaging that aspect. I get interested with every announcement from Level99 who are almost the opposite - I couldn't care less for the Indines lore, but the mechanics of the games tend to be rock-solid (A Brad Talton/>G crossover would be EPIC!). Will I still be excited going forwards with a >G release? Maybe, but with a real hint of caution.

That said, I like the niche this game is aimed at, the idea of a Sentinel themed party game definitely appeals, the idea of a story based one also, but not this one. At all.

I have real issues with party games that can be meta-gamed - Cards Against Humanity, Dixit, and I believe Apples to Apples have the winners decided without knowing who will be gaining points (beyond real guess-work of what sort of card a player may play). This one (and games like Say Anything where people write their answers) provides a player the option to select the winner which may be player who they want to win/don't want to win ("You never pick me!" etc), or the one that poses least threat.

As for storytelling games, Gloom is a framework upon which you enhance the game by the storytelling. Once Upon A Time, the story has to fit how you shed cards (if I recall correctly), so there is some structure for less confident people to work with. This one feels way to thin, and too dependant on performance. I hope I'm wrong, but I'm pretty much ruling out being on the kickstarter for this!
